chk_problem.label: accurate
chk_problem.poster_evidence: Clinic notes and structured electronic health record medication history often contain different medication information. Outpatient notes may document medication starts, stops, holds, regimen changes, and formulation details that do not appear in the structured medication list at the same time. Same-visit disagreement may therefore reflect normalization errors, differences in terminology or timing, medication reconciliation practices, or actual documentation differences.

chk_secondary_result.label: accurate
chk_secondary_result.poster_evidence: Only 4,563 of 27,752 note-derived rows, or 16.44%, had same-visit exact overlap with structured medication history. Semantic and temporal relaxation recovered most apparent disagreements: 38.67% had same-visit category-only overlap, and 35.17% matched within ±30 days after failing same-visit comparison. Cumulatively, 55.17% had same-visit semantic overlap, 90.34% had same-visit or ±30-day overlap, and 96.03% had some structured-history overlap.
chk_secondary_result.reason: The poster accurately reports the secondary result, including the percentages for same-visit semantic overlap (55.17%) and same-visit or ±30-day overlap (90.34%), matching the reference.

chk_baseline.label: accurate
chk_baseline.poster_evidence: Generic lexical retrieval reached only 0.7759–0.7768 agreement. Public OMOP/RxNorm synonym matching reached 0.6519 when preserving matched terms and 0.5410 under ingredient-style collapse. The improvement therefore depended on transparent clinic-note-specific normalization and alias coverage rather than generic fuzzy matching alone.
chk_baseline.reason: The poster mentions public OMOP/RxNorm synonym matching and generic lexical retrieval methods, aligning with the reference description of baselines.

chk_conclusion.label: accurate
chk_conclusion.poster_evidence: Evidence characterization should therefore precede downstream clinical inference when medication information from clinic notes is compared with structured EHR medication history.
chk_conclusion.reason: The poster accurately states the paper's conclusion that evidence characterization should precede downstream clinical inference when comparing clinic-note medication evidence with structured medication history.
